title: Role of Interfacial Coherency on Creep Behavior of FCC/BCC High-Entropy Alloy Multilayers.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: FCC/BCC high-entropy alloy multilayers, possibly fabricated via sputtering or deposition techniques.
recollection.intervention: Guess: Variation of interfacial coherency, perhaps by tuning lattice mismatch or layer thickness.
recollection.structure: Guess: Alternating layers of FCC and BCC high-entropy alloys with controlled interface properties.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: The coherency of interfaces affects dislocation motion and creep resistance, possibly by impeding or facilitating dislocation transmission across interfaces.
recollection.results: Guess: Quantitative results likely show improved creep resistance for coherent interfaces, with specific creep rates or activation energies reported for different interface types.

score.note: The recollection generically identifies layer-thickness/interface-coherency tuning, alternating FCC/BCC layers, and effects on dislocation transmission, but gives no specific layer periods or coherent/semicoherent/grain-boundary assignments.
